anti_overlap: fd-crisis-communications-director covers FEED's institutional messaging patterns
fd-behavioral-economics-researcher covers default enrollment and complicity psychology
decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where the perceptual split would collapse into a simple information-access game (higher faction rep = more data) rather than an analytical challenge (multiple framings of the same data require judgment). The breach mechanic should feel like all-source analysis, not just unlocking a second camera angle.
distance_rationale: Intelligence analysis deals with exactly the same core problem — integrating reports from sources with different biases about the same events — but is a professional discipline with centuries of formalized methodology.
expected_isomorphisms: All-source analysis with incompatible framings maps to the perceptual RPG. Source reliability profiling maps to FEED distortion calibration. The cost of source-crossing operations maps to breach economics.
focus: Whether the perceptual RPG system and breach mechanic produce genuine analytical sophistication rather than simple information access
name: fd-intelligence-analysis-tradecraft
persona: An intelligence analyst trained in all-source analysis — integrating reports from sources with different biases, access levels, and reliability ratings. Thinks in terms of source evaluation, analytical confidence, and the cognitive cost of maintaining multiple competing hypotheses about the same event.
review_areas: Check whether 'same data, different framing' (Meyrowitz model) actually produces analytically distinguishable situations or if the framings are just cosmetic variations on the same interpretation

Assess whether the breach mechanic requires genuine analytical effort (cross-referencing, evaluating source reliability, maintaining competing hypotheses) or just data access (see both layers simultaneously)

Verify that the Calvino faction themes (Trade, Signs, Dead, Eyes, Desire) produce sufficiently distinct analytical lenses that a player seeing all five simultaneously would need to resolve contradictions, not just read more text
Check whether the 'forced breach events' (async MMO world events that crack the divide) produce lasting analytical consequences or are just temporary information leaks

Evaluate whether the FEED distortion system creates the kind of source-reliability assessment that intelligence analysts perform — can players learn to calibrate FEED's credibility on a per-axis basis?

severity_examples.condition: No document specifies how the perceptual layers CONTRADICT each other — they are described as different emphases, not conflicting claims
severity_examples.scenario: Breach reduces to 'now I can see the Stakeholders layer too' rather than 'now I must reconcile two incompatible accounts of the same event'

severity_examples.condition: All five faction framings interpret 94% supply as either 'good' or 'bad' with no genuine disagreement about what the data means
severity_examples.scenario: The Calvino framings are aesthetically distinct but analytically redundant — they all reach the same conclusions through different vocabulary

source_domain: Intelligence Analysis Tradecraft and All-Source Analysis
success_hints: A breach player should face genuine analytical dilemmas: two faction framings that reach opposite conclusions from the same data, forcing the player to evaluate which framing is more reliable for this specific situation

FEED's distortion should be calibratable — a skilled player should be able to estimate the true value from FEED's reported value by understanding the distortion function, like an analyst correcting for known source biases
task_context: The perceptual RPG system uses Mieville's City & The City model: same city, different perception based on faction alignment. Breach lets players see multiple layers but at a cost. The Invisible Cities framework maps each faction to a Calvino observation theme.
